mission: Re-test J-ADV-1 ADV1-V05 P2 claim: 14 image upload requests use mimes (extension) not mimetypes (magic byte) — assess polyglot / double-extension / SVG XSS / DoS / RCE risk

static_analysis: grep -rn 'mimes:' app/ — catalog every FormRequest + inline validation
Read public/.htaccess + public/file/.htaccess for Apache stack

empirical_probe.harness: /tmp/l71-probe/probe.php, probe2.php, probe3.php, probe4.php — standalone PHP loading vendor autoload, instantiating Illuminate Validator + Spatie FileAdder via reflection
fixtures_built: A_shell.php — polyglot JPEG header + <?php system($_GET[c]) ?> in EXIF comment, named shell.php
D_shell.pht — same polyglot, .pht extension (NOT in blocklist)

stack_facts.spatie_file_namer: DefaultFileNamer (preserves client filename + extension; no UUID/random rename)
stack_facts.spatie_default_sanitizer: preg_replace('#\p{C}+#u','',name); str_replace(['#','/','\\',' '],'-',name) — strips control bytes (including \x00) and replaces path separators; dots and tabs after strip become '-' substitution
stack_facts.spatie_disk: MEDIA_DISK env, defaults to 'public' (= storage/app/public, web-exposed via storage/symlink → public/storage)
stack_facts.image_optimizers_enabled: Jpegoptim --strip-all (strips EXIF in conversions), Svgo, Pngquant, Optipng, Gifsicle, Cwebp, Avifenc — BUT optimizers run on derived conversions, not on the originally stored 'original' media file
stack_facts.webserver_targeted_for_le_cayenne_V1_loc: Apache (.htaccess exists) AND nginx (deploy templates exist) — V1 LOCAL likely Apache box; V2 cloud cutover will use nginx vhost templates

extension_only_validations: ALL 16 catalogued validations use `mimes:` (extension-derived) — 0 use `mimetypes:` (magic-byte derived)
ItemRequest, ItemCategoryRequest, ChangeImageRequest, CouponRequest, MessageRequest, OfferRequest, SliderRequest, PageRequest mimes:jpg,jpeg,png
ThemeRequest (3 fields) mimes:jpg,jpeg,png — NO max:size set

j_adv_1_p2_claim_reconciliation.claim_was: 14 image upload requests use `mimes:jpg,jpeg,png` (extension-derived) not `mimetypes:image/jpeg,...` (magic-byte). Polyglot + double-extension RCE depends on nginx PHP-exec block in /storage/*
j_adv_1_p2_claim_reconciliation.verdict_on_claim: PARTIALLY ACCURATE — mimes-only count confirmed (16 incl. xlsx/json), BUT the framing missed two Laravel-level defenses that materially change the risk surface
laravel_defenses_observed_empirically: Laravel validateMimes uses $value->guessExtension() which calls Symfony MimeTypeGuesser (finfo_file content-based) and maps MIME → extension — so the extension list IS effectively magic-byte-validated against image content for the JPEG/PNG/SVG family (empirical: a polyglot with JPEG bytes returns guessExtension()='jpg')

Laravel's shouldBlockPhpUpload() explicitly REJECTS getClientOriginalExtension() in [php, php3, php4, php5, php7, php8, phtml, phar] REGARDLESS of content (added in Laravel 9.2 — present in this repo via vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Validation/Concerns/ValidatesAttributes.php:1483-1496)
remaining_gaps_after_defenses: shouldBlockPhpUpload blocklist MISSES: .pht, .php2, .php6, .phps, .phpt, .phtm, .module, .inc — these are configurable PHP-handler extensions in some webserver setups
Double extension shell.php.jpg PASSES validation (extension=jpg) AND Spatie's defaultSanitizer DOES NOT strip the .php middle segment — saved on disk as 'shell.php.jpg' verbatim
Null-byte truncation: client filename 'shell.php\x00.jpg' is stripped by sanitizer to 'shell.php.jpg' (control bytes removed) — same exposure as plain double extension

PushNotificationRequest.php:37 — rule `'mimes:jpeg,png,jpg|max:5098'` inside a flat array element is NOT split into two rules by Laravel's parser (verified empirically). Laravel treats it as a single mimes rule with extensions ['jpeg','png','jpg|max:5098']. The max:5098 is NEVER applied. 10 MB+ files accepted → DoS vector bounded only by nginx client_max_body_size 25-32MB and PHP post_max_size
ThemeRequest (theme_logo/theme_favicon_logo/theme_footer_logo): no max:size set at all — bounded only by webserver limits

Spatie stores under the public disk (storage/app/public symlinked into public/storage). nginx vhost templates have a global `location ~ \.php$` block with NO exclusion under /storage/ — meaning IF an attacker ever managed to drop a stored filename ending in literal .php under storage/app/public, PHP-FPM WOULD execute it. The Laravel guards above currently prevent that filename from being stored, but the defense-in-depth gap is real

exploit_vectors_found.title: .pht extension bypass on RCE
exploit_vectors_found.description: Polyglot JPEG-magic file uploaded as shell.pht passes ItemPhotoUploadRequest, ItemRequest, ItemCategoryRequest, ChangeImageRequest, OfferRequest, SliderRequest, MessageRequest, PageRequest, CouponRequest. Spatie persists literal 'shell.pht' under storage/app/public/N/. nginx PHP regex `\.php$` does NOT match `.pht`, so it does NOT execute under standard nginx. BUT: if the deploy ever uses Apache with `AddHandler application/x-httpd-php .pht` (default-OFF, but admin-toggleable), or if a future ops change widens the PHP regex to `\.ph` or `\.ph(p|t)`, RCE becomes live. Mitigation: extend shouldBlockPhpUpload blocklist via custom validator OR add nginx `location ~ ^/storage/.*\.(ph|pht|phps|phtm|inc)$ { deny all; }`.
exploit_vectors_found.proof: TEST_1 D_shell.pht → PASS validation; TEST_3 sanitizer preserves 'shell.pht'
preconditions: admin user with permission:items_edit (or peer item/category/etc. perm)
webserver configured to exec .pht as PHP — NOT default on lecayenne-prod nginx, MUST verify Apache stack

exploit_vectors_found.title: Double-extension persistence (shell.php.jpg → defense gap)
exploit_vectors_found.description: Files named shell.php.jpg pass all validations and are stored on disk with literal name 'shell.php.jpg' under /storage/app/public/N/. nginx default `\.php$` regex does NOT match (ends in .jpg). BUT: Apache with `AddType application/x-httpd-php .php` + default mod_mime multi-extension handling (`Options +Indexes` style configs from cPanel/shared-hosting era) WILL execute files with `.php` anywhere in their extension chain. The Le Cayenne V1 LOCAL stack uses Apache (public/.htaccess exists), and the current vhost does not explicitly deny PHP handler invocation on multi-extension files under /storage/.
exploit_vectors_found.proof: TEST_1 B PASS, TEST_3 shows literal name preserved
mitigations_in_place: public/storage Spatie disk → NOT served by app PHP code (direct static)
Apache mod_php auto-handler typically NOT installed on a Laravel-only PHP-FPM box
exploit_vectors_found.hardening_recommendation: Add to public/.htaccess: `<FilesMatch "\.ph(p[345678]?|t|tml|ar|ps)\.">` Require all denied `</FilesMatch>` (denies any path containing .php* before a dot)

exploit_vectors_found.title: PushNotificationRequest |max:5098 parser bug → DoS
exploit_vectors_found.description: Rule at app/Http/Requests/PushNotificationRequest.php:37 is `'image' => ['image', 'mimes:jpeg,png,jpg|max:5098']`. Laravel's array-form rule parser does NOT split a sub-element on `|` — the max:5098 is parsed as a fake extension `'jpg|max:5098'` and the size limit is NEVER enforced. Empirically, a 10 MB valid PNG passes. With nginx client_max_body_size 25-32 MB and PHP post_max_size typically 32 MB, an authenticated admin can upload 30 MB notification images repeatedly → storage exhaustion + Spatie image-conversion queue saturation.

exploit_vectors_found.title: ThemeRequest absent max:size → DoS
exploit_vectors_found.description: app/Http/Requests/ThemeRequest.php:27-29 — three image fields (theme_logo / theme_favicon_logo / theme_footer_logo) declared as `['nullable', 'file', 'mimes:jpg,jpeg,png']` with NO max:size. Bounded only by nginx client_max_body_size (25-32 MB) and PHP post_max_size. Each upload spawns Spatie image-conversion derivatives (thumb/cover/preview) — 3 large simultaneously = sustained CPU + storage hit.
exploit_vectors_found.proof: ThemeRequest.php:27-29 source — no max key in any of the three rule arrays
exploit_vectors_found.fix: Add 'max:2048' (2 MB) to each of the three rules — consistent with other image FormRequests

exploit_vectors_found.title: shouldBlockPhpUpload blocklist incomplete (no .phps/.phpt/.phtm/.inc)
exploit_vectors_found.description: Laravel 9.x shouldBlockPhpUpload covers php/php3-8/phtml/phar but misses .phps (PHP source display), .phpt (PHP test), .phtm, .inc (commonly included PHP). On stacks where any of these are configured as a PHP handler, the polyglot+content-magic bypass is live. .phps in particular is widely configured to display source — could leak any /storage-uploaded content as PHP source (mild infodisclo).
exploit_vectors_found.fix: Override validateMimes via a custom FormRequest base class or register a custom validator that extends the blocklist

vectors_blocked_or_safe: SVG XSS (E_xss.svg) — BLOCKED by mimes:jpg,jpeg,png[,webp] on all 14 image FormRequests (svg not in allowlist). The 'image' rule alone WOULD accept it, but every endpoint pairs 'image' with 'mimes:' restriction
Direct shell.php upload — BLOCKED by shouldBlockPhpUpload
Path traversal '../../../etc/passwd.jpg' — BLOCKED by Spatie defaultSanitizer (/ and \ replaced with -)
Null-byte injection in filename — null is stripped by Spatie sanitizer; reduces to L7.1-V2 (double-ext case, same risk surface)
Firebase service-account JSON exposure — HARDENED by GOAL-HEAL-SEC-001 (firebase_private non-public disk + public/.htaccess + public/file/.htaccess + nginx-deny-sensitive-files.conf)
Excel ZIP-bomb auto-extraction — Maatwebsite uses ZipArchive on-demand for XLSX read, not full disk-extract; max:2048 on import requests bounds initial upload to 2 MB

ItemService::addMediaFromString file_get_contents($path) at line 681 — $path is the source path of a previously-validated uploaded image being re-attached during item-photo cleanup. Not user-controllable URL. Safe.

nginx_apache_exec_block_assessment.nginx_vhost_template: scripts/deploy/nginx.conf.template:163-175 — `location ~ \.php$` is global (matches /storage/.../*.php). NO `/storage/` exclusion. If a .php file ever lands under public/storage, PHP-FPM executes it. Currently dependent on Laravel guards preventing storage.
nginx_apache_exec_block_assessment.apache_htaccess_protection: public/.htaccess + public/file/.htaccess — deny credential bundles (.pem/.key/.json/etc.) but DO NOT explicitly deny .php/.phtml/.pht under /storage. Defense-in-depth gap.
missing_hardening: nginx: add `location ~ ^/storage/.*\.(ph|pht|phps|phtm|inc|cgi|pl)$ { deny all; }` BEFORE the global `\.php$` block
apache: add to public/.htaccess: `<FilesMatch "\.(ph|phtml|phps|phtm|inc|cgi|pl)$">` Require all denied `</FilesMatch>`
Pin Spatie file_namer to a UUID-rename custom FileNamer to remove client-extension persistence entirely (eliminates V2 + most of V1)

rce_risk_assessment:
CURRENT VERDICT: LOW-but-NON-ZERO on a hardened stack, MEDIUM if any Apache mod_mime multi-extension handler is enabled.

Rationale:
1. Laravel shouldBlockPhpUpload prevents the obvious shell.php path
2. Laravel guessExtension content-checks JPEG/PNG/SVG magic bytes — naive polyglot rejected for SVG, accepted only when extension+content both align with image
3. Spatie sanitizer does NOT rename to UUID — original client extension chain persists on disk → enables V1 (.pht) and V2 (double-ext) IF the webserver maps those to PHP
4. nginx default vhosts here do NOT explicitly deny PHP under /storage — defense-in-depth gap that becomes live RCE only if (a) an extension exec-mapping change ships OR (b) shouldBlockPhpUpload is bypassed via some future Laravel core regression
5. PushNotification |max bug + Theme no-max = real DoS surface today on authenticated admin endpoints (medium-impact, attacker-must-authenticate)

recommendations_for_hardening.fix: PushNotificationRequest.php:37 — change `'mimes:jpeg,png,jpg|max:5098'` to separate array elements `'mimes:jpeg,png,jpg', 'max:5098'`. One-line surgical fix, no frozen-zone touch. Add unit test.
ThemeRequest.php:27-29 — add `'max:2048'` to each of the three image rules. Aligns with all other image FormRequests.

Add custom validation rule (or FormRequest base trait) that extends shouldBlockPhpUpload blocklist to include pht, php2, php6, phps, phpt, phtm, inc, module — applied to all *Request files via composition. Also add a sentinel test enforcing the extension list.

Pin Spatie file_namer to a custom UUID-prefixed FileNamer that uses Symfony MimeTypes::getExtensions($mimeFromMagicBytes) — fully eliminates client-supplied extension persistence. Drop-in: extend DefaultFileNamer, override originalFileName() and conversionFileName().
recommendations_for_hardening.blast_radius: high (changes file_name column values for new uploads — does NOT migrate existing records; coordinate with frontend that references file_name)

recommendations_for_hardening.fix: nginx vhost — add BEFORE `location ~ \.php$`: `location ~ ^/storage/.*\.(ph|pht|phps|phtm|inc|cgi|pl|html|htm)$ { deny all; access_log off; log_not_found off; }`. Apply to both scripts/deploy/nginx.conf.template (lecayenne) and deploy/ansible/templates/nginx-foodking.conf.j2.
recommendations_for_hardening.blast_radius: trivial vhost change, validated with nginx -t before reload

recommendations_for_hardening.fix: Apache: add to public/.htaccess: `<FilesMatch "\.(ph|phtml|phps|phtm|inc)$">` `<IfModule mod_authz_core.c>Require all denied</IfModule>` `</FilesMatch>` — recursive deny applies to public/storage symlink target
recommendations_for_hardening.blast_radius: trivial, double-check no legitimate file uses these extensions in public/

recommendations_for_hardening.fix: Switch mimes: rules to mimetypes: rules where possible (e.g. `mimetypes:image/jpeg,image/png,image/webp`) for explicit magic-byte enforcement. Laravel's validateMimetypes uses Symfony MimeTypeGuesser regardless, but the explicit name makes the intent auditable.

verdict_rationale: Laravel 9.x shouldBlockPhpUpload + Spatie content-aware validation + nginx default `\.php$`-only regex collectively prevent immediate RCE on the current Le Cayenne V1 LOCAL stack. However: (a) PushNotificationRequest.php:37 rule-parsing bug is a confirmed DoS vector requiring 1-line fix; (b) ThemeRequest missing max is parallel DoS surface; (c) shouldBlockPhpUpload blocklist gap (.pht/.phps/etc.) + Spatie not renaming files = ambient defense-in-depth weakness that turns live RCE the moment any extension-handler config shifts. NOT a V1 ship-blocker, but the two P1 fixes should land before cloud cutover.
